editorial:
Imagine being head-over-heels for your best friend, but he has no idea you're even interested. That is exactly where Laurent finds himself. He shares a flat with Dan, a total playboy who is completely straight. Just when you think Laurent is okay with being just friends, Dan falls for a girl named Camille. Now, the movie turns into a wild ride as Laurent tries every trick in the book to break them up. He is not alone for long, though, as he teams up with his new lesbian roommate, Sam, and his buddy Nick to stop the wedding. It is a funny, messy situation that feels like a classic comedy of errors where everything that can go wrong actually does.

You will love how the energy stays high and the jokes land well. The acting feels natural, and the chemistry between the roommates makes the drama feel real even when things get ridiculous. While some of the plots are a bit predictable, the way they play out is still a blast. If you are in the mood for something light and romantic, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the colorful French scenery.
endingExplained: After all the chaos and failed attempts to stop the wedding, things take a surprise turn. Camille realizes that Dan is not the right match for her, and she actually develops feelings for Laurent. The movie wraps up with a twist where the original plan to save Dan fails, but Laurent finds true love with Camille instead. Everyone ends up happy and the fight for marriage equality provides a sweet, hopeful backdrop to the final scenes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic comedies and stories about friendship and mistaken identity.
